description.value: The study reassessed an existing sample to examine whether a history of DSM-IV-TR-assessed withdrawal modulates neural reactivity biases to drug-related versus food-related reward cues in cocaine-dependent participants.

spans.text: The current study offers insight into these conflicting positions by using secondary analyses to assess how a history of DSM-assessed withdrawal influences the magnitude of bias in neural reactivity to drug- and/or food-related reward cues.

design.value: Secondary analyses of an existing sample comparing cocaine-dependent participants with and without a history of withdrawal to a non-dependent control group during an fMRI cue-reactivity paradigm.

spans.text: The present study involved a reassessment of the results, to carefully evaluate the influence of withdrawal status on the magnitude of biases in neural reactivity to drug-related and food-related stimuli.

description.value: Lifetime withdrawal status was determined from two parent questions and confirmation of dysphoric mood plus at least two withdrawal symptoms.

### Cue-elicited craving task

task_description.value: Participants viewed cocaine-related and food-related videos during two identical runs.

spans.text: Participants were presented with two identical runs during which they viewed 29 videos (duration: ∼10,000–14,000 ms): 15 videos depicted individuals preparing or using cocaine, and 14 videos depicted individuals preparing or eating food.
Videos were separated by an inter-trial jitter of either 2000, 3500, or 5000 ms to aid deconvolution from the standard hemodynamic response function.
